featured_reviews.name: SAMS TRAVELOGY
featured_reviews.review_text:
@bombayisland #Samstravelogy Rating 🌟🌟🌟🌟/5
The Ambience: Raw & Educational
​The vibe here is refreshingly industrial and transparent. The space is strategically partitioned into functional zones: one counter dedicated to the art of the pour, a roasting station, and a grinding section. Seeing the entire process—from bean to cup—happening live in-store adds a layer of authenticity that is rare to find. It’s a sensory experience where the aroma of roasting beans sets the stage for what’s to come.
​The Drink: A Masterclass in Fusion
​While the menu is expansive and full of curiosities, the Dirty Matcha Coffee is a standout. It is truly outstanding—balancing the earthy, grassy notes of high-quality matcha with the bold, acidic kick of a well-pulled espresso shot. The textures were seamless, proving that the baristas here aren't just making drinks; they are executing technical maneuvers with precision.
​The Verdict
​Though the food menu is surprisingly large and tempting, the coffee remains the undisputed star of the show. Whether you are a casual drinker or a "true-blue" coffee aficionado, the specialized preparation techniques used here are impressive.
​I’ll definitely be returning to explore the food offerings, but for now, the coffee alone makes this a must-visit spot in the Vikhroli neighborhood.

featured_reviews.name: Purple R
featured_reviews.review_text:
I came across Ringo on social media and decided to give it a shot.

The atmosphere is undoubtedly the highlight. The view overlooking The Trees is peaceful, and the cafe itself has a relaxed, laid-back vibe. where you can easily spend an afternoon with a book from their collection and a cup of coffee. If I happened to be in the area, I'd happily stop by for the ambience alone.

Unfortunately, the service left a lot to be desired.

When I ordered the Vietnamese coffee, I asked for the condensed milk to be served on the side. The staff member taking my order seemed oddly reluctant, and what should have been a simple request turned into an unnecessarily awkward interaction. After confirming that the condensed milk wasn't pre-blended, I requested it separately, only to receive a rather strange "as you wish" in response.

To make matters worse, the coffee itself had a burnt, slightly sour taste. It made me wonder whether the condensed milk was intended to mask the flavour. The cold brew, however, was excellent and easily the best drink we tried.

Another odd moment came when a staff member was walking around spraying air freshener while guests were eating. It wasn't a major issue, but it felt out of place in a cafe where aroma is such a big part of the experience.

We also experienced a surprisingly long wait for our order. Since this is a pay-first, order-at-the-counter setup and most of the menu consists of bakery items, the delay felt longer than expected. What made it more noticeable was seeing several customers who appeared to order after us receive their food much sooner.

Food-wise, we sampled quite a few items:

Crab Rangoon Roll (6/10)
The filling didn't quite work for us. It felt under-seasoned and lacked the flavour we were expecting.

Jerk Chicken Bun (7.5/10)
Our favourite item of the visit. The filling had great flavour and oddly reminded us of a spicy keema pav. The only downside was the bread-to-filling ratio.

Mulberry Danish (7/10)
This was one of the items we were most excited about. Visually it looked fantastic, but the filling leaned more towards whipped cream than the richer custard-like filling I was expecting. While pleasant enough, it felt lighter and less satisfying than anticipated

Double Chocolate Brioche (8/10)
Rich, indulgent, and hard to dislike if you're a chocolate lover.

Almond Croissant (6/10)
Too sweet and surprisingly dry, with a filling that felt a little off balance.

Egg Masala Puff (7/10)
A pleasant surprise. The flavours were well executed and it stood out more than expected.

Overall, Ringo is a beautiful cafe with a relaxing atmosphere and a strong cold brew, but the food didn't quite live up to the setting and the service felt oddly cold throughout the visit. I'd stop by again if I happened to be nearby, but I wouldn't make a special trip across Mumbai for it.

Unfiltered Café – Unfiltered Review ☕⚠️

First visit. First impression. Disappointing.

For a new café with a young team, enthusiasm is visible—but training, service processes, and management oversight are clearly missing. If the vision is to grow big and create a standout customer experience, management needs to be far more hands-on at this stage.

What works:
✔️ Thoughtfully designed space
✔️ Two well-defined seating sections
✔️ Good table spacing – great for co-working or long coffee chats
✔️ Calm, aesthetically pleasing vibe

What doesn’t:
❌ Pricing is on the higher side for the location
❌ Portion size vs pricing doesn’t quite add up
❌ 45 minutes wait for a single dish (won’t name it)
❌ After that wait, the dish was… average at best

That kind of delay, especially when the café isn’t packed, kills the experience completely.

One saving grace:
✔️ Chicken Bibimbap – genuinely good and recommendable.

Final take:
Would I return? Maybe for coffee and ambience. Not for food.

There’s potential here—but execution, speed, and consistency will decide whether this place survives or fades away.

Best wishes to the management—the concept is strong, now the operations need to catch up.

featured_reviews.name: Blue Beacon Maverick
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a hardcore non-vegetarian like me, a "mostly vegetarian" menu usually wouldn't be your first pick. But Unfiltered, located right on LBS Marg next to R-City Mall, might just change your mind. It’s a refreshing addition to Vikhroli, saving you that long trek to Powai or Godrej for a high-quality cafe experience.
Here is the breakdown of what I tried:
The Food & Coffee
The menu is versatile, featuring everything from croissant sandwiches to hearty bowls. While it’s veg-forward, they offer the option to add chicken to most dishes.
* Chicken Club Sandwich (7/10): A solid, dependable choice. The ingredients were incredibly fresh and the chicken was perfectly tender. It’s "just a sandwich" at the end of the day, but they execute it well.
* Mushroom Cigar Rolls (8/10): These were crispy and packed with umami flavor. The only downside? The sweet chili dip. The rolls are savory and earthy, and the sweet sauce felt like a bit of a mismatch.
* Green Garden Sandwich (9/10): Surprisingly, this fully vegetarian sandwich was a highlight. It was fresh, incredibly filling, and proved you don’t need meat for a satisfying meal here.
* Burnt Vanilla Coffee (10/10): I’ll be honest, I didn't get a strong hit of vanilla, but I didn't care. It was strong, fresh, and perfectly balanced.
The Showstopper: Hot Chocolate
Rating: 11/10 (if that’s allowed)
Forget the watered-down cocoa powder you get elsewhere. This is melted chocolate in a bowl. It is thicker than a bowl of tomato soup and decadently rich. It’s definitely meant to be shared, though I didn’t, and I have zero regrets. This alone is worth the trip.
Ambience & Vibe
The cafe has a bit of a split personality when it comes to decor:
* Outdoor/Non-AC: A beautiful tropical vibe that feels very "cafe-esque."
* Indoor/AC: A bit of a departure from the tropical theme; it feels more like the interior of a traditional South Indian restaurant. It’s comfortable, but a slightly different mood than the exterior.
The Verdict
Overall: This place is a winner. The freshness of the ingredients shines through in every dish.

I’ll definitely be back, and I’m already recommending it to friends. I really hope these folks stay in business for a long time, Vikhroli needs a spot like this!
